comment: Operations whose status changed since the last tag and that the release note
deliberately does not name, each with the reason (#326).
The default is to name them. `tools/release/surface.sh` computes what changed
from the committed coverage artefacts of the two tags, and prints the list
ready to paste into CHANGELOG.md — which is the release body, extracted
section by section by .github/workflows/release.yml. This file is for the
operation a note would be worse for carrying, and it costs a sentence.
- an entry with no reason is refused, because "not worth naming" is a
decision somebody signs rather than a silence with a filename;
- an entry that excuses nothing in the current window is refused, because a
stale exemption is a gate that quietly stopped covering what it names.
tools/compat/accepted.json lives under the same rule and fired on it the
The second rule has a consequence worth knowing before it surprises anybody:
the window is `latest tag → working tree`, so an entry written for a release
excuses nothing once that release is tagged. Emptying this file is a step of
RELEASING.md, right after the tag is pushed.
